messages:
Maria Chen: ran a quick end-to-end on staging for the kernel handoff change + tokenbudget sampler. saw a ~12% p95 regression on short prompts when the handoff threshold moved from 64->80 tokens. not blocked but want eyes.
Aj Patel: thanks — is that across all kernels or specific to xform-8fp16->xform-4q?
Maria Chen: mostly on the xform-8fp16 -> xform-4q path. long prompts unaffected. suspect we increased context-switch overhead for tiny batches. logs attached below.
Devon Brooks: can you paste the profiler snippet? curious about memcpy vs compute time.
Maria Chen: profiler snippet (filtered):
```
TIMESTAMP  op            ms  tokens
12:03:22   matmul_k         1.2   48
12:03:22   memcpy_cpu_gm    0.9   48
12:03:22   kernel_switch    2.5   48  <-- candidate hotspot after handoff
12:03:22   kv_lookup        0.3   48
```
Maria Chen: the kernel_switch row jumps when the sampler triggers the handoff for workloads with decode_rate > 25 tok/s and prompt_length in [8,64].
Sai Kannan: interesting. we tuned the sampler to be aggressive to avoid long latency tails for midlen prompts. might be overshooting on very small batches.
Lina Gomez: do we have the token-budget config we used?
Maria Chen: config snippet we ran on staging: 
```json
{"token_budget_target": 120, "soft_budget_fraction": 0.8, "handoff_threshold_tokens": 80, "decode_rate_bins": [10,25,50,100], "kv_warmup_ms": 20}
```
Aj Patel: soft_budget_fraction 0.8 means we try to form batches up to 96 tokens before forcing a handoff, right?
Devon Brooks: yep. so with short prompts (like 16 tokens) that results in ~6-7 requests queued before flush. that increases kernel_switch overhead if we switch runtime/kernels per batch.
Maria Chen: exact. also saw increased KV eviction churn during high-concurrency runs — kv_warmup_ms=20 might be too low for quantized kernels.
perf-bot: perf-ci: regression detected on staging job 2026-03-18T12:02 — p95 latency +12% for model redwood/gptx-1-small-q4 on short_prompt_suite
Sai Kannan: for isolation: can we test a variant where handoff_threshold_tokens=64 and token_budget_target=80 but increase kv_warmup_ms to 60? hypothesize kernel switches remain cheaper if KV warmup reduces misses.
Lina Gomez: also try a decode_rate-aware gate: only allow handoff when decode_rate_bin >= 2 (i.e., >25 tok/s). that avoids moving small, slow prompts.
Aj Patel: good call. I can spin two ABs: A) revert threshold to 64 + kv_warmup_ms=60, B) keep 80 but add decode_rate gate. quick commands:
```bash
# AB A
curl -X POST http://staging/api/params -d '{"handoff_threshold_tokens":64, "kv_warmup_ms":60}'
# AB B
curl -X POST http://staging/api/params -d '{"handoff_threshold_tokens":80, "decode_rate_min_bin":2}'
```
Devon Brooks: please also log kernel_id and batch_size at handoff boundary, append `hand_off_meta` field — we need to know if we're flipping to a slower kernel for small decode widths.
Maria Chen: added hand_off_meta logging patch in PR #2412 — it logs kernel_id, prev_kernel_id, batch_size, kv_hit_rate.
Sai Kannan: another angle: reduce kernel selection frequency by adding hysteresis on kernel selection decisions (only switch if candidate kernel is 10% faster on recent window). prevents flapping.
Lina Gomez: +1. that should tame rapid switches for midriff workloads.
Aj Patel: timeline — spin ABs now, let them run for 2 hours, then collect p50/p95 and kv_hit_rate. I'll post results.
Maria Chen: thanks. quick note: saw a weird interaction — when token_budget_target was high (200) on the same handoff change we actually improved throughput by ~8% for midlen prompts because batching grew but ks overhead amortized. so tradeoff is workload dependent.
Devon Brooks: makes sense. for throughput-focused workloads push token_budget_target up; for latency-critical ones keep it low + gating. we should add per-route defaults in console.
perf-bot: perf-ci: ab-variant A started job 2234506891, variant B started job 2234506892
Maria Chen: action items:
- Aj: run ABs and share p50/p95 + kv_hit_rate (2h)
- Devon: add hysteresis knob to kernel selector + tiny perf test
- Sai: prototype decode_rate_min_bin gating in sampler
- Lina: note recommended defaults in console per-route settings
I'll follow up with combined graphs. thanks all :thumbsup:
Aj Patel: on it.
Devon Brooks: will open PR for hysteresis today.
Sai Kannan: prototyping now.
Lina Gomez: will draft defaults doc after results.
Maria Chen: leaving logs and raw profiler in the staging workspace Slack thread — link pinned above.
